review.summary: The v2 proof satisfies every applicable item of the production standard and reproduces none of the predecessor's registered defects. The headline states the point without teasing; the opening answers what happened, the audience boundary and the action in under 90 words before any technical term; all five planned numbers carry units, exact first-use sentences, point-of-use attribution to Panfilov and colleagues (August 2026), and reconcile to the source map including the 328-files-versus-704-details unit warning and the unstated real-people denominator. The extraction attack is defined in plain language before being named, the recovery method precedes the dependent result, paragraph breaks separate changed bases and precede the 64-of-704 comparison, terminology is locked to two stable object terms with the predecessor's rotating metaphors prohibited, the central instruction has exactly three permitted jobs with prohibited restatements, and the 550-word four-section Daily plan gives one ACTION section sole ownership of imperatives.
review.formatJob: The Daily in REPORT_OR_ANNOUNCEMENT mode genuinely governs the shape: a dated research finding with one immediate sharing lesson, planned at 550 words within the 350–700 band, with an explicit routing reason deferring deeper technical-safeguard treatment to another lane. The four-section plan (MECHANISM, EVIDENCE, EXAMPLES_ONLY, ACTION) follows the mode's required order — plain answer and background first, mechanism cause by cause, evidence limits, applications, then action — and each section has one distinct reader job with no generic scaffold headings.
review.plainOpening: The headline "Shared AI work files carried passwords — and details the chat never showed" states the news factually without danger inflation or withheld subject. The roughly 60-word opening answers before any jargon: a study found passwords and private details in published AI work files, some invisible in the chat; ordinary private chats were not shown to be exposed; the lesson is for anyone sharing AI work. A cold reader can state the point from the opening alone, which the rejected predecessor failed.
review.causalTeaching: The six-link outline is causes, not labels: the tool keeps a visible answer plus the sealed part; publishing the work file carries both; during the test period a less-protected sibling model could be made to reveal what the sealed part represented; that exposed details some of which never appeared on screen; disclosure stopped the attacks; sharing only the checked answer avoids the mismatch. The mechanism bridge names where the invisible object lives, defines the attack in plain language before the shorthand "extraction attack," and states how the evidence was recovered before the results that depend on it.
review.evidenceBoundary: The proof states both sides in reader language: the preprint establishes real passwords, keys and personal details in sampled public work files (328 of 6,708 files, 4.9%; 704 distinct details after the real-people filter; 64 sealed-only), with the demonstrated attacks reported stopped after disclosure. It does not establish that private consumer chats were published, that every work file leaks, that the attacks still work, or that every recovered word is exact, since the researchers lacked the original hidden text. The changed group and unit between 328 and 704 is stated plainly, and no denominator is invented.
review.readerUse: Both applications are concrete and distinct: at work, a coding assistant diagnosing a broken website may see a deployment key (glossed as a code that can publish site changes) that rides in the work file; at home, a travel assistant connected to email produces a shareable itinerary while the work file carries account details. The landing is direct and transferable — choose and check the answer you intend to send rather than publishing the work file by default — with a separate incident action assigning carriage to the file: treat any published credential as exposed, rotate it, and know deletion cannot undo copies.
